behaviors.behavior: AC1: an empty-content reply is retried and a later success wins
AC1: retries exhaust and the leg reports degraded
AC1: the degraded-reply retry count is budgeted by llm_client.max_retries (configured N -> N+1 attempts)
AC1: llm_client.max_retries is wired into the OpenAI() client constructor (real transport-level retry)
AC1: a negative configured max_retries is clamped to zero rather than reaching the SDK negative
AC1: max_retries defaults sanely when config omits it
AC1: the direct-OpenAI path (no OpenRouter key) shares the same retry behavior
AC1: a truncated/cut-off reply (finish_reason) is retried the same as an empty reply
AC2: one degraded leg alongside a succeeding leg is reported as partially_degraded with the failing leg named
AC2: a partial degradation prints a loud stderr warning
AC2: total degradation (every leg failed) does not ALSO report partially_degraded
AC2: a merely-skipped leg (no API key / no route) is not counted as a partial degradation
AC3: a degraded leg auto-files a deduped triage card
AC3: filing is idempotent within the dedup window (no duplicate card on repeated failures)
AC3: no triage card is filed when every leg succeeds
AC3: a triage-filing failure never breaks the review gate's own exit code
AC3: one leg's filing failure does not suppress filing for another leg
